newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH M/M CPI FALLS 0.2 PCT IN JULY - FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: POLISH M/M CPI FALLS 0.2 PCT IN JULY - FINMIN.

text.p: Polish month-on-month consumer price index fell 0.2 percent in July, against a 1.5 percent rise in June, finance ministry preliminary data showed.
"According to our preliminary estimates prices in July fell 0.2 percent, which means inflation was -0.2 percent. The fall could have been bigger if not for the floods," Belka told a news conference.
He did not say how the 0.2 percent estimated inflation fall would affect the year-on-year index, which was at 15.3 percent in June.

The government wants to bring inflation down to 13 percent in December, but the central bank and independent economists have said July's floods, the worst in centuries, made that goal increasingly difficult to achieve.

To finance flood relief efforts the government already borrowed one billion zlotys from the central bank and may borrow a further 1.5 billion by the end of the year, which economists say is the most inflationary way of raising cash.
